chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said:

I asked him about salat at night and during the day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars can be seen. He said: 'Exert your judgment and deliberately aim for the Qibla to the best of your ability.'

key_terms.اجتهد رأيك: Exert your judgment — exercise personal reasoning and effort to determine the Qibla
key_terms.الشمس والقمر والنجوم: The sun, moon, and stars — traditional celestial markers used to determine prayer direction
key_terms.الصلاة: Salat — the obligatory ritual prayer, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.القبلة: Qibla — the direction of prayer toward the Ka'ba in Mecca
key_terms.جهدك: To the best of your ability — Islamic legal principle that obligation is commensurate with capacity

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when they cannot see the sun, moon, or stars to determine the Qibla direction for prayer?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran asked Imam al-Kazim (AS) about performing prayer when celestial navigation markers — the sun, moon, and stars — are all obscured, such as during heavy clouds or fog. The Imam's response establishes a practical legal principle: in the absence of any means of determining the Qibla direction, a Muslim must exercise personal judgment (ijtihad al-ra'y) and make their best effort to face the Qibla. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic legal maxim that obligation is measured by capability, and sincere effort suffices when certainty is unattainable.
word_analysis: to the best of your ability
